newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF seen halting some Nomura operations -- report.
newsitem.headline: MOF seen halting some Nomura operations -- report.

text.p: Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) is likely to suspend some of Nomura Securities Co Ltd's operations, including stock dealing on its own account, for about three months as a penalty for a scandal linking it with "sokaiya" racketeers, the news service of the Mainichi Shimbun reported on Tuesday.
Mainichi reported that the penalty would be the heaviest ever imposed on a securities firm in Japan.
A formal decision on the penalty will be made by the ministry after it receives recommendations from Japan's securities watchdog, it said. It did not quote any sources in the story.
Mainichi also said that the penalty on Nomura could be even heavier, depending on the outcome of the Tokyo prosecutor's ongoing investigation.
A MOF official declined to comment on the report.

The Mainichi said the suspension would likely keep Nomura from engaging in new share public offering operations and thus affect its stock dealings on behalf of clients, dealing a heavy blow to its business.
Earlier on Tuesday, former Nomura president Hideo Sakamaki told a parliamentary committee that the brokerage paid more than 70 million yen via stock deals into accounts linked to a former racketeer.
Sakamaki stepped down last month to take the blame for the scandal.
The Mainichi said the tough penalty would be based on the fact that two Nomura directors were involved in the deals and that the payoffs occured over a long period of time.
The two directors resigned after Nomura admitted they were involved in the deals.
